blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A method returns shipping labels: `return shipments.stream().mapMulti((s, out) -> { if (s.express()) out.accept("EXPRESS " + s.id()); out.accept(s.id()); }).map(String::toUpperCase).toList();`, and its declared return type is `List<String>`. `Shipment` is a record with `String id()` and `boolean express()`. What does javac do with this method?

options.text: It compiles it, since the String values passed to out.accept make the stream a Stream<String>
options.says: javac doesn't infer mapMulti's result type from what the lambda body passes to accept

options.text: It rejects it, since nothing names what mapMulti emits, so the next stage gets a Stream<Object>
options.says: R appears only in the type of the lambda's parameter; with another call after mapMulti, R becomes Object and String::toUpperCase doesn't apply

options.text: It compiles it, since the declared List<String> return type makes every stage a Stream<String>
options.says: the target type doesn't reach back through the calls that follow mapMulti; it decides R only when mapMulti is the last call

options.text: It rejects it, since out.accept may be called only once per element of a Stream<Shipment>
options.says: mapMulti's function may call accept any number of times, zero included

origin.section: mapMulti Emits Zero or More Results Without a Stream per Element, but javac Can't Infer What It Emits

questions.stem: A roster service orders a ward's shifts with `shifts.stream().sorted().toList()`, where `Shift` is `record Shift(String nurse, LocalTime start) {}`. Its unit test sorts a list holding one shift; in production the call gets the eight shifts of a day. What happens?

options.text: Production throws at toList(), and the one-shift test doesn't, since only comparing two shifts needs Comparable
options.says: a non-Comparable element fails at the terminal operation when the sort compares two; one element is never compared

options.text: Production throws at toList(), and the one-shift test does too, since the sort checks each shift as it takes it in
options.says: nothing checks the elements until two are compared; a stream of one sorts without complaint

options.text: Production throws at sorted(), and the one-shift test doesn't, since the stage checks the type only for several elements
options.says: building the pipeline checks nothing: the exception comes from the terminal operation

options.text: Production throws at sorted(), and the one-shift test does too, since the stage checks the type when it is built
options.says: the page's run prints 'pipeline built' before the exception, which comes from toList(); one element doesn't throw at all

origin.section: filter and map Pass Each Element On; sorted Holds Every Element Before It Emits One

questions.stem: Checkout collects coupon codes with `carts.stream().flatMap(c -> c.coupons() == null ? null : c.coupons().stream()).map(Coupon::code).toList()`. Of three carts, the first holds two coupons, the second is a guest cart whose `coupons()` is null, and the third holds one coupon. What does the call give?

options.text: A list of three codes, since the stream treats a null from flatMap's function as an empty stream
options.says: the javadoc says an empty stream is used in place of a null mapped stream; the page's run shows it

options.text: A NullPointerException in map(Coupon::code), since flatMap passes the null on to the next stage as an element
options.says: that is what map does with a null result; flatMap uses an empty stream instead

options.text: A NullPointerException inside flatMap, since flatMap reads the elements of whatever stream its function returns
options.says: flatMap checks for null and uses an empty stream

options.text: A list of three codes, since toList() leaves out the null elements that reach it
options.says: toList() keeps null elements, as the map run on the page shows ([pen, null, pad])

origin.section: map Gives One Result per Element; flatMap Splices a Stream per Element into One

questions.stem: A trading screen's `trades()` returns a `Stream<Trade>` that ends only at market close. At 10:00, the screen calls `trades().filter(t -> t.quantity() > 10_000).sorted(Comparator.comparing(Trade::price)).findFirst()` to show the cheapest block trade. By 10:00, several block trades have already arrived on the stream. What does the screen get, and when?

options.text: Nothing until market close, since sorted can't emit its first element before it has seen the last
options.says: sorted is stateful: it buffers every element and emits only when the source is exhausted, so findFirst after it stops nothing upstream

options.text: The cheapest block trade so far, at once, since findFirst stops the pipeline as soon as it has an element
options.says: a short-circuiting operation after sorted stops nothing upstream: sorted pulls every element first

options.text: The cheapest block trade so far, at once, since sorted orders what has arrived when the stream doesn't end
options.says: sorted never emits before the source is exhausted; on an endless stream it never returns

options.text: Nothing until market close, since findFirst needs the whole stream before it picks an element
options.says: findFirst stops after one element, as the trace with sorted shows (one 'after sorted' line); the wait comes from sorted

origin.section: filter and map Pass Each Element On; sorted Holds Every Element Before It Emits One

concepts: A null returned by flatMap's function is treated as an empty stream, while a null returned by map's function stays in the stream as an element.

mapMulti emits zero or more results through a Consumer, and when another call follows it javac needs the result type as a type argument or typed lambda parameters, or the stream becomes a Stream<Object>.
sorted() on elements that aren't Comparable throws ClassCastException at the terminal operation, and only once two elements are compared.
